Goldens/vectors are self-produced by the implementation-under-test. This file
is how a PR carries an INDEPENDENT justification for changing one. Every entry
pins a specific golden file to the exact NEW content it is authorizing, via a
sha256 of that file's bytes. Because the pin is content-addressed, an entry can
only ever justify the ONE value it was reviewed for — a later, different
regeneration of the same file fails the gate again and forces a fresh entry.
See conformance/README.md -> 'Golden-regeneration integrity gate' for the full
design and the two ways to satisfy the gate.
Schema of each entry in `entries`:
path             (string, required)  repo-root-relative path of the golden file
sha256           (string, required)  hex sha256 of the file's NEW (post-change) bytes
verified-against (enum,   required)  one of: official-KAT | second-implementation |
differential-oracle | intentional-spec-change
reason           (string, required)  human explanation of WHY the new bytes are correct
and against WHICH independent oracle they were checked
reviewer         (string, required)  sign-off marker, e.g. a GitHub handle 'gh:alice'
date             (string, optional)  ISO date the entry was added
To compute the sha256 of a golden after you have regenerated it:
shasum -a 256 conformance/tests/<fixture>/expected-script.hex
or run the checker with --print-hashes to get them for the whole changed set.
